About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The Role

As Technical Delivery Lead, EMEA, you will own how Legora's customers across the region go live and scale. You will lead and grow a team of Technical Delivery Managers who run end-to-end implementations, from SSO to document-management integrations, and you will stay close enough to the work to step into the projects yourself.


This is a player-coach role. You set the delivery standard for EMEA, make sure every customer has a clear path from kickoff to adoption, and act as the link between the delivery team and Sales, Customer Success, Engineering and Product. You will also help shape the delivery playbook as Legora keeps expanding across the region.

What You'll Do

Lead the EMEA delivery team

  • Manage, coach and develop a team of Technical Delivery Managers across EMEA, including hiring, onboarding and performance

  • Allocate projects across the team based on complexity, customer priority and capacity, and keep workloads sustainable

  • Set clear expectations for quality, timelines and customer communication, and hold the team to them

Own delivery outcomes for the region

  • Oversee the pipeline of integration projects from kickoff through go-live, and step in early when a project is at risk

  • Act as the senior technical escalation point for complex implementations, including SSO, authentication, and document-management integrations

  • Track delivery metrics such as time to go-live, project health and customer satisfaction, and report on them to leadership

  • Stay hands-on with select strategic customer projects

Build the delivery engine

  • Standardise how EMEA delivers: playbooks, technical documentation, test plans and rollout checklists that the team can reuse

  • Improve how delivery hands off to support, Customer Success and adoption teams after go-live

  • Work with global delivery leads so that practices stay consistent across regions while reflecting local customer needs, such as data residency and regional security requirements

Work across the business

  • Partner with GtM and Solutions Engineering on scoping and technical feasibility before deals close, so commitments made to customers can be delivered

  • Work with Engagement and Legal Engineering to turn successful go-lives into lasting adoption

  • Bring patterns from delivery projects back to Engineering and Product to influence the roadmap and make future implementations easier


Who You Are

  • Proven experience in technical delivery, implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role, including at least 2 years leading or managing a team

  • Strong hands-on background with enterprise integrations and implementation

  • A track record of running multiple parallel implementation projects with a structured, proactive approach to blockers and risk

  • Experience building repeatable delivery processes, not only running individual projects

  • Able to translate technical concepts clearly for non-technical audiences, including senior customer stakeholders

  • A strong communicator who builds trusted relationships across customer and internal teams

  • A coach who gives direct, useful feedback and helps people grow

  • Comfortable working autonomously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

  • Based in, or willing to relocate to, one of our EMEA hubs, with the flexibility to work with customers across European time zones

Nice to Have

  • Experience delivering software to law firms, in-house legal teams or other regulated, security-conscious customers

  • Familiarity with SSO, iManage, SharePoint or similar document management platforms

  • Experience with EMEA data residency, GDPR and enterprise security review requirements

  • Fluency in one or more European languages in addition to English

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

data.description:
Qdrant is an open-source vector search engine powering the next generation of AI applications, from semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to AI agents and real-time recommendations.

Trusted by global leaders like Canva, HubSpot, Tripadvisor, Bosch, and Deutsche Telekom, we’re building the retrieval infrastructure layer for modern AI. Recently raising $50M in Series B funding, we are growing rapidly and committed to transforming how AI understands and interacts with data.

As a remote-first company, we believe diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences fuel innovation. Here, you’ll own meaningful work, tackle challenges, and grow alongside passionate individuals dedicated to shaping the future of AI.

The Team and Your Impact

Hi, I'm Gio, and I lead People & Culture at Qdrant. I joined in April 2026 to build the People function from scratch. We have laid the foundations: went live with Ashby and with a new HRIS, launched our first engagement survey, a leveling framework, and our first review and compensation cycles are coming in 2027.

Our colleagues are spread across about 30 countries, and our People team is small by design. We need systems that scale as Qdrant does. As our Senior People Operations Engineer, you’ll build how People Ops runs, write the policies behind it, and automate every process that doesn’t need a human touch.

You don't need "People Operations Engineer" in your title to apply. If you are an HR generalist who automates everything, or an HR systems person who has handled multi-country cases, we want to hear from you.

What you will own

About 60% of your time goes to running People Ops, and about 40% to building. The mix will shift with what the business needs. Your first year has four main areas:

  • AI-native People Ops

    • Use Claude and MCP frameworks every day to build agents and automations that take repetitive work off the team, starting with request triage and policy questions

    • Get the process and documentation right before you automate it, and decide what should stay human

    • Share what you learn, so the rest of the team picks up the same tools

  • People platforms, data, and analytics

    • Own our HRIS and people stack, including integrations, access, and data quality

    • Build people analytics and reporting, and work with me to turn the data into decisions leadership can act on, from attrition and engagement trends to headcount planning

  • Global employment and payroll

    • Lead our move to a single global payroll provider, replacing today’s mix of US PEO, EOR, and local payroll setups with one platform, and make sure employment contracts, visas, and Finance coordination carry through the transition without gaps.

    • Design onboarding, mobility, and offboarding so they work the same way in every country

    • Be the go-to person for tricky cases like relocations, with external counsel behind you

  • Policies and benefits

    • Own our employee policies end to end, from drafting and legal review with counsel to rollout and upkeep

    • Design and launch a global benefits offering, country by country

    • Build a self-service documentation library, so people can find answers without asking

Who you are

  • You've spent 5 or more years in People Ops, HR operations, or People Systems, including time in a scaling, remote-first People function with EU and US presence

  • You've employed people in several countries across entities, EOR, and freelancers, with hands-on US and EU experience, and you know how to keep it compliant

  • You've worked with EOR, PEO, and global payroll platforms and can spot what looks off in payroll inputs before it goes out

  • You've owned an HRIS and people stack hands on, from setup to integrations and data quality, and you have real people analytics experience

  • You have strong Claude and Claude Code skills and use AI and MCP daily. You've built agents, skills, automations, or integrations that took real work off a team, ideally on HR or business systems. You know how to use AI with people data safely and in line with GDPR

  • You know your way around HR and automation tools: ideally Ashby and Leapsome (or HiBob, Greenhouse, or Personio), Deel or Remote, Jira, and n8n, Zapier, or Make

Nice to have

  • Comfort with APIs, webhooks, or light scripting

  • Knowledge of German or Spanish employment law, and a working grasp of US labor and employment rules

  • You have built a benefits offering across countries or consolidated EOR and payroll vendors

This role is probably not for you if you:

  • Need to be told what to fix first, or wait for a playbook before deciding

  • Want the process designed before you run it

  • Would rather someone else figure out the solution, and just implement it

  • Struggle with ambiguity and change. We're scaling and adapting as the market evolves, so priorities will shift

  • Prefer a quick call to writing things down, since we work async first

Interview process

  1. A 45-minute call with me (Gio). We talk about Qdrant, the role, and your background, and I am your point of contact throughout.

  2. A practical exercise: show us how you’d approach a real People Ops challenge

  3. Technical interviews:

    • A deeper conversation with me and the team (45 min)

    • A call with another colleague, so you get to know us too (30 min)

  4. A final call with one of our leaders.

I review every application myself after the application deadline, so take the time to tell us why you're a fit!

Why join us

  • A remote-first, international team working on cutting-edge AI infrastructure.

  • A competitive salary with additional perks.

  • Flexible working hours and async-friendly culture.

  • High ownership and real impact.

  • Open-source, engineering-driven culture.

  • Choose your own laptop equipment.

For US-based full-time employees, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package including 401k match, health, dental, and vision insurance, plus flexible PTO policy.


Qdrant is an equal-opportunity employer. We believe the best ideas come from diverse teams, and we actively welcome applicants from all backgrounds. If this role excites you but you don't check every single box, we'd still love to hear from you! We don't want to miss out on great people because of a checklist.

Come build with us!


For information on how we handle your personal data, please refer to our Recruitment Privacy Policy

We work with over 5,000+ teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes' health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.  

Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS

We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to help build, operate and improve the infrastructure, platforms and tools that enable our teams to develop, deliver and run reliable software at scale.

Based in Cologne, you will join a team with broad ownership of our technical environment. We take a cloud-agnostic approach, combining cloud services and self-hosted infrastructure to meet the needs of our products and engineering teams. Our responsibilities span the full lifecycle, from provisioning and deployment to observability, security and ongoing operation.

You will combine infrastructure expertise with automation and software engineering to improve how our software is built, deployed and operated. This includes streamlining development workflows, integrating and maintaining shared tools, and supporting demanding workloads across data processing, media and machine learning. Working closely with engineering teams and colleagues across the business, you will build practical solutions that support our expanding product portfolio.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving a wide range of technical problems, takes ownership from initial idea through to production, and thrives in a fast-growing environment where priorities and requirements evolve quickly. You will help shape how our infrastructure, platforms and tools adapt as the business grows.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Design, operate, and continuously improve our Kubernetes platform across both self-hosted clusters and AWS
  • Own our infrastructure as code using Terraform and Ansible, driving a GitOps workflow to ensure all changes are versioned, reviewed, and reproducible
  • Build and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI) and shared templates that empower product teams to build, test, and deploy reliably
  • Operate and scale specialized infrastructure for demanding workloads, including GPU clusters for computer vision models, media engines, and data analytics platforms 
  • Evolve our observability stack to proactively monitor system health, define meaningful alerting, and ensure high availability
  • Drive platform security and compliance through continuous vulnerability scanning, automated image screening, robust secrets management, and strict access controls
  • Collaborate closely with software engineers, data scientists, and product teams to design scalable architectures and act as a strategic technical partner for new infrastructure initiatives 

Help define technical direction, engineering best practices, and quality standards within the infrastructure domain 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 5+ years of professional experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Platform Engineering, with a proven track record of designing and scaling highly available production environments 
  • Strong hands-on experience running Kubernetes in production, including upgrades, networking and troubleshooting
  • Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure (AWS) combined with experience operating bare-metal or self-hosted environments

Proven experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) and modern container build or GitOps workflowsStrong problem-solving skills and the ability to evaluate technical trade-offs between reliability, scalability, and maintainabilityExperience collaborating across engineering and product teams to deliver secure and robust infrastructure solutionsDeep understanding of Linux operating systems and strong programming or scripting skills (e.g., Python, Go, or Bash) focused on automation and tooling. 

Nice to have – and what would make you exceptional:

  • Experience operating GPU workloads on Kubernetes or Machine Learning infrastructure
  • Familiarity with specialized Kubernetes ecosystem tools such as FluxCD, Rancher, or RKE2.
  • Experience working with large-scale video/streaming workflows or AWS media services
  • Experience managing and scaling messaging or event-streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) 
  • Experience operating and optimizing relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL) 
  • Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling for engineering teams

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • In 6 months time… You know our clusters and pipelines, handle incidents and upgrades on your own, and have shipped your first improvements to reliability, automation or security. You contribute confidently to architecture discussions.
  • In 12 months time… You own major parts of the platform, have delivered measurable improvements (faster deployments, better observability, stronger security), and help shape the roadmap of our hybrid cloud.

WHY CATAPULT? 

  • We have amazing people. We promise you'll work with some of the most ambitious,  intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
  • We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary. 
  • We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
  • Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.  
  • We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve.  There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

Whether you're interested in sports or not, you'll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet! 

Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized groups tend only to apply when they check every box. So if you have what it takes, but don't meet every single point in our job ad, please still get in touch! We would love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team. We are building the future of sports performance. Our priority is to find the brightest talent who can add to our team culture, actively contribute, and be excited about what they do.

All offers of employment are subject to Catapult's positive prehire check. To find out more, please contact the Talent Partner for this role.

Engineering Manager - Platform and Data Intelligence

 
 

About trawa

 

European energy costs are 2x compared to US and China. Electricity demand is expected to double by 2050. Market price volatility & complexity are here to stay. The backbone of Europe's industrial economy is at risk and companies need to act now.

trawa is building the solution: the first integrated B2B energy platform that orchestrates procurement, energy management, and flexibility steering in one product. Supply, Manage, and Flex combined. That integration unlocks up to 30% in recurring electricity cost savings, all while helping companies switch to renewable energy.

We're the fastest-growing B2B energy platform in Europe. Active in Germany and Austria now, and expanding operations to a third market in 2027. We're on the road to European scale and move fast, the market window is open and we intend to own it.

trawa is a scale-up based in Berlin with ~100 FTE, ~30 of whom work in Product & Tech. We've raised over €35M to date, including a €24M Series A in May 2025, backed by Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic, and Tiny VC. All three founders are on board and 100% committed to build the utility of the future.

 
 
 

About the Role

 

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead two teams that form the foundation everything at trawa runs on: Data Intelligence and Platform.

Data is the heartbeat of trawa. It turns the complexity of energy markets into savings and sustainability for our customers. Underneath it sits the cloud infrastructure powering our services and the IT and security practices that keep our systems and data safe. You’ll own the technical direction for all of it, from metering data management and billing to AWS infrastructure and internal IT.

You’ll shape a team culture grounded in trust, collaboration, and continuous learning, where engineers thrive and do their best work. You’ll report to the Director of Engineering and lead an established, growing group of engineers across two closely related teams.

At trawa, our culture is “office-first with flexibility”: most of us are in our Berlin office the majority of the week, with room to work from home when needed. The Tech team follows a more hybrid rhythm, with a minimum of 3 days a week in the office.

 
 

What You'll Do

 

Own the roadmap for our central data warehouse and the data platform our products are built on

  • Build a scalable data backend for the core processes of an energy provider, including timeseries data management, invoicing, and billing

  • Lead the design and operation of critical data pipelines, data quality standards, and observability practices

  • Run scalable, secure, highly available infrastructure on AWS for our mission-critical services

  • Drive great developer experience through CI/CD, observability tooling, and internal platforms that help teams ship faster and with confidence

  • Own IT operations and security: the tools, processes, and policies that keep trawa’s systems and data safe

Our tech stack

  • AWS, Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions

  • Postgres, ClickHouse, dbt, Metabase

  • Python (pandas, polars), TypeScript

  • Dash0, Sentry, incident.io

  • Primo

 
 
 

Your First 90 Days

 

First 6 weeks (onboarding)

  • Build strong relationships with your direct reports, peers, and stakeholders

  • Understand each team’s current OKRs and how they impact the company

  • Get a solid understanding of our data architecture, infrastructure, and security posture

By month 3 (ramp-up)

  • Review operational health and tech debt across both teams, and present a prioritized plan for improvements in observability, data health, and scalability

  • Define and share a clear vision and roadmap for Data Intelligence and Platform, including how we improve developer experience

  • Assess our IT operations and security practices, and plan how they scale with trawa’s growth

  • Align next quarter’s roadmap with stakeholders and company OKRs, and communicate it broadly

 

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years in a technical leadership role with people management responsibilities, ideally in a fast-moving startup. You’ve led across multiple teams and know how to balance competing priorities.

  • Deep hands-on background in data platform/data engineering or platform engineering/SRE/DevOps, and solid working knowledge of the other

  • Strong AWS experience: infrastructure as code, cloud-native patterns, containerized systems, with a good grasp of security, reliability, observability, and cost efficiency

  • Clear communicator who builds trust across teams and with non-technical stakeholders

  • Inclusive leader who creates an environment where engineers of diverse backgrounds can thrive

Don’t meet every single requirement? We still encourage you to apply!

At trawa, we’re dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to apply – you may be the right fit for this or another opportunity.

 
 
 

Why Join Us

 

🌍 Real impact - At trawa, you will be part of a team that is dedicated to making a positive impact on the world. We value creativity, collaboration, and diverse perspectives.

 

🚀 Early ownership - We empower our team members to take ownership of their work and drive results, regardless of background or experience level.

 

🤝 Mentorship that matters - Regular leadership sessions, cross-functional exposure, and engineers who are genuinely invested in your growth.

 

📚 Learning culture - We provide an annual budget and dedicated time for professional development. You’ll have opportunities for mentorship, learning, and career progression.

 

🌐 Inclusive by design - We’re an equal opportunity employer, and our team reflects that. Our tech organisation brings together over 15 nationalities, contributing a variety of languages, experiences, and perspectives. At trawa, we’re family-friendly with parents across all levels, and our diversity is represented throughout the company, including leadership. We’re committed to an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

 

🎁 Solid benefits - We offer a competitive compensation package including salary and stock options, 30 days of vacation, and a range of benefits including subsidies for home internet and lunches, a Sports Club membership, a productivity budget for work essentials (e.g., headphones, monitor), dedicated learning days with an annual learning budget, plus a weekly team lunch and regular team events.

Bewerbungen nehmen wir ausschließlich über unsere Website entgegen. Dort sind es zehn Fragen, deine Kontaktdaten und der Arbeitsvertrag – alles in einem Ablauf, ohne Lebenslauf und ohne Anschreiben.

Fragen zur Stelle beantworten wir dagegen gern per E-Mail an ----- uns

Probantica ist ein Anbieter für Qualitätstests aus Köln. Wir prüfen im Auftrag von Unternehmen, ob digitale Produkte und Abläufe vor Ort im Alltag funktionieren. Die Tests machen bei uns angestellte Qualitätsmanager:innen – Menschen mit Vertrag, feste Ansprechperson und klaren Vorgaben.

Worum es geht

Unternehmen müssen wissen, ob ihre Apps, Websites und Filialen im Alltag wirklich funktionieren. Als Kunde gehst du die angebotenen Abläufe durch: App öffnen, Konto anlegen, Formular ausfüllen, Bestellung abschließen, in eine Filiale gehen. Du testest den Prozess von Anfang bis Ende, dokumentierst jeden Schritt mit Uhrzeit und Screenshot und markierst die Stellen, an denen etwas hakt oder unklar bleibt.

Vor jedem Auftrag bekommst du eine Anleitung mit Schritten, Zeitrahmen und den Fragen, die am Ende beantwortet sein müssen. Kein Rätselraten, kein Vertrieb, keine Kaltakquise. Getestet wird auf deinem eigenen Gerät, in deiner Nähe.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Digitale Produkte testen: App, Website oder Online-Prozess einmal vollständig durchlaufen – von der Anmeldung bis zum Abschluss.

  • Abläufe vor Ort prüfen: in Filialen, Shops oder Servicestellen, mit Blick auf Wartezeit, Beratung und Abwicklung.

  • Auffälligkeiten festhalten: Screenshot machen, Uhrzeit notieren, in zwei bis fünf Sätzen beschreiben, was passiert ist.

  • Bericht einreichen: die vorgegebenen Fragen beantworten, Dauer je Schritt angeben, Ergebnis knapp zusammenfassen.

  • Nachfragen beantworten: wenn das Team zu einem Befund etwas wissen möchte, kurz und sachlich antworten.

Das bringst du mit

  • Du bist mindestens 18 Jahre alt.

  • Du hast ein Smartphone oder einen Laptop mit Internetzugang – Geräte für App- und Website-Tests stellst du selbst.

  • Du drückst dich in klaren, verständlichen Sätzen aus und arbeitest sorgfältig.

  • Du hältst Termine ein und meldest dich, wenn etwas nicht klappt.

Das brauchst du nicht

  • Kein Studium, keine Ausbildung in einem bestimmten Bereich, kein Führerschein.

  • Keine eigene Firma, keine Anmeldung beim Finanzamt.

  • Keine Kosten – weder für die Bewerbung noch für die Ausrüstung.

Vergütung pro Auftrag

Feste Pauschale je abgeschlossenem Auftrag, gestaffelt nach Umfang. Ausgezahlt wird monatlich, sobald der Bericht abgenommen ist – unabhängig davon, wie lange du gebraucht hast.

  • Kleiner Ablauf (Anmeldung, Formular, eine Seite) – ca. 60 Minuten – 19 €

  • Großer Ablauf (Konto, Antrag, mehrere Schritte) – ca. 90 Minuten – 29 €

  • Filiale vor Ort (inkl. Anfahrt) – ca. 120 Minuten – 39 €

  • Sonderauftrag (mehrere Geräte, mehrere Termine) – ca. 150 Minuten – 49 €

Richtwerte. Das konkrete Honorar steht in jedem Auftrag, bevor du ihn annimmst. Die Pauschale ist so bemessen, dass der gesetzliche Mindestlohn für die aufgewendete Zeit nicht unterschritten wird.

Das bieten wir dir

  • Faire Pauschale – bis zu 49 € pro Auftrag, monatlich ausgezahlt, ohne Provision und ohne Abzug.

  • Anstellung statt anonymer Crowd – Arbeitsvertrag und feste Ansprechperson statt Bewertungsplattform.

  • Minijob oder Teilzeit – Minijob bis zur Geringfügigkeitsgrenze (2026: 603 € monatlich), Teilzeit bis 20 Stunden pro Woche.

  • Flexible Einteilung – du sagst, wann du Zeit hast; keine festen Schichten.

  • Klare Vorgaben – jede Aufgabe mit Anleitung, Zeitrahmen und den Fragen für den Bericht.

  • Persönliche Begleitung – im Panel erreichst du deinen Supervisor direkt, ohne Ticket-System.

  • Kurzer Weg – Bewerbung in etwa zehn Minuten, Rückmeldung meist innerhalb von zwei Werktagen.

So läuft die Bewerbung

  1. Zehn Fragen beantworten (etwa 5 Minuten) – online, ohne Anmeldung, ohne Lebenslauf.

  2. Persönliche Daten eintragen – Name, Anschrift, Geburtsdatum, Kontaktdaten.

  3. Rückmeldung per E-Mail – bei einer Zusage kommen die Zugangsdaten für dein Panel mit.

  4. Arbeitsvertrag digital unterschreiben – Minijob oder Teilzeit.

  5. Onboarding im Panel – kurze Einführung, danach die ersten Aufträge.

Gut zu wissen

  • Keine Provision: bezahlt wird der abgeschlossene Auftrag, nicht die Anzahl gefundener Fehler.

  • Keine Vorkasse, keine Kaution, kein Verkauf an Freunde oder Familie.

  • Du bestimmst, wie viele Aufträge du übernimmst – es gibt keine Mindestanzahl.

  • Alle Geschlechter willkommen. Schwerbehinderte Bewerber:innen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt.

This immersive, hands-on role involves daily collaboration with lab and controls engineers in a cleanroom, requiring precision, adherence to

What You'll Do

3D Environment Artist & Level Designer
ScapeWorld Entertainment · Remote

  • Level: Senior to lead

  • Location: Remote, CET overlap

  • Contract: Full time, long term

About us

We are ScapeWorld Entertainment, a fully remote Swedish game studio of just over 20 people. We are building Scape, a platform of multiplayer games where a player’s identity carries across all of them. We have just launched our first game within Scape. Our senior team has shipped and run live games at studios including Arrowhead (Helldivers 2), Avalanche Studios and Ubisoft.

The project

Our next game is a cleaning and restoration sim set in a shared neighbourhood. Every player has a place of their own that starts buried in junk and grime, and puts it in order in full view of neighbours who are doing the same.

Cleaning games are usually played alone or in short co-op sessions. We want to make one set in a neighbourhood that players share and keep coming back to, and we want to do it well. We have a working prototype and are refining the loop now. If you play games like this and have views on what makes them satisfying, you will enjoy this.

About the role

We are looking for a senior to lead 3D environment artist who is also a level designer.

You will be the only level designer on the project. You own the game’s spaces, from first layout through to dressed and lit, and you are responsible for delivering them.

The role is split roughly evenly between environment art, mostly props and other environment 3D assets, and level design, which includes some gameplay design. On the design side you work with our Creative Director and engineering, and you bring your level and gameplay design experience into those discussions. On the art side you work with the rest of the art team.

You report to the Art Director.

What you will do

Environment art

  • Model and texture props and other environment 3D assets. Most of what we use is made in-house, and we also work with asset packs where they fit.

  • Work to our polygon, texture and material standards. Assets used in large numbers, such as foliage, are kept low poly. Most props use standard poly counts.

  • Build modular kits that can be reused across levels.

  • Dress and light levels in Unity, following the Art Director’s visual direction.

Level design

  • Design the layout of rooms and plots: how the player moves through them, what they notice first, and the order in which the space is revealed as it is cleared.

  • Greybox levels and take them through to final, checking scale, pathing and collision in engine.

  • Test levels in engine and in playtests, and make changes based on the results.

  • Help shape how spaces support the game loop and its features, and give input on pacing and progression.

  • Document your work: layout plans, kit guides and dressing guidelines.

What we are looking for

  • Senior to lead level, with several years of professional experience in game development.

  • Experience as both an environment artist and a level designer. You have done each on at least one project, shipped or not, and you have owned a game’s spaces or levels from start to finish.

  • Some gameplay design experience, for example working on game loops, features or mechanics alongside level layouts.

  • A portfolio that shows both sides: real-time environments and 3D assets you made, and levels you designed, from greybox to final.

  • Good working knowledge of Unity, including building and lighting levels. Our level tools are built inside Unity.

  • Comfortable using Blender. It is part of our production pipeline, and we have built an add-on for it.

  • Comfortable using the Substance suite for texturing and materials.

  • Comfortable giving your view in design discussions and explaining your reasoning.

  • Able to work independently from a brief, and to work closely with a small team.

  • Comfortable working in English every day, in meetings (mostly on camera) and in writing. It does not need to be perfect.

Nice to have

  • 3D character or gameplay animation.

  • 3D character modelling.

  • Technical art or VFX.

  • Experience with GitHub or Fork.

  • Experience with player-built levels, or tools for game creators.

  • Experience in a small team where you covered more than one role.

What we offer

  • A fully remote team with flexible working.

  • Trust to manage your own time. We do not use timesheets.

  • Ownership of the game’s spaces, from first layout to final.

  • A small team where people help each other.

Working setup

  • Fully remote. Your working day needs to overlap with CET.

  • Full time, on a long-term contract. It is business to business.

  • We would like you to start as soon as you are available.

What this role is not

  • Not a lead game designer role. Our Creative Director sets the direction of the game.

  • Not an art-only or design-only role. You will do both.

How to apply

Apply through the link; a few short questions are part of the application form. If we shortlist you, the next step is interviews, and for final candidates an unpaid planning task of about two hours at an agreed time, with no modelling or texturing. We reply to everyone at every step.

Disclosure

This application will be evaluated with the help of an AI tool that checks your CV and application against the criteria for this role. A human recruiter always makes the final decision. The AI does not reject or accept anyone on its own. If your application isn’t taken forward, you can ask us for an explanation of how the AI was used in that decision. See our Candidate Privacy Policy below for full details, or contact us at

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About TRM

TRM Labs is on a mission to build a safer world by fighting crime and protecting the people who investigate it. We started as a blockchain intelligence company, helping law enforcement, government agencies, financial institutions, and businesses detect, investigate, and disrupt crypto-enabled crime. Today our platform reaches well beyond the blockchain: we fuse on-chain data with cyber and open-source intelligence (OSINT) so investigators can move from a single crypto address to the full story behind a criminal network. Our blockchain intelligence and AI intelligence platforms turn fragmented signals into fast, defensible investigative leads for the teams protecting public safety and national security every day.

TRM Academy delivers training and certification for the global community of investigators, analysts, and compliance professionals who detect and prevent fraud and financial crime involving cryptocurrencies. Learners get live and virtual courses, practical exercises, and a community of the world's experts in blockchain, crypto compliance, and financial crime investigations.

About the Role

As the Lead Instructor, EMEA, you will own the design and delivery of TRM Academy training across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, with blockchain intelligence and crypto investigations at the core of what you teach. You will turn complex on-chain concepts into practical, mission-ready skills for law enforcement, national security, and government audiences, and you will be equally comfortable teaching crypto businesses, exchanges, and financial institutions. Cyber and OSINT tradecraft is the complement: you will show investigators how to pair it with on-chain tracing to build a complete case.

EMEA is a region where we win by showing up. You will deliver in person, in the room, with customers across the UK, DACH, the Nordics and Baltics, France, and beyond, and you will work closely with our regional sales, value engineering, and customer success teams so that training drives adoption and opens the next conversation. You will join a Training Team of master instructors who can command a room, build engaging content, and speak to every level of expertise. We know how our products are used in the real world and help our customers become humble masters too.

This is also a build role. EMEA training is a growing opportunity, and you will help shape how it is scoped, packaged, and delivered as the region scales.

Please note: this role requires travel of 50-75%, primarily across EMEA.

The Impact You'll Have Here

  • Program manage and deliver live, in-person, and virtual blockchain intelligence training to law enforcement, national security, and government learners across EMEA.

  • Teach crypto fundamentals through advanced investigations on TRM's blockchain intelligence and AI intelligence platforms, helping investigators trace funds and build complete, defensible cases.

  • Develop and maintain curriculum, labs, and practical exercises that stay current with the crypto threat landscape, including fraud, scams, ransomware, hacks and exploits, terrorism finance, sanctions evasion, and money laundering typologies.

  • Adapt content for regional legal frameworks, case types, and audience maturity, from first-time crypto investigators to experienced national security analysts.

  • Pair on-chain tracing with cyber and OSINT techniques in courses and case walkthroughs, so learners can pivot from off-chain signals to blockchain activity.

  • Partner with sales, value engineering, and customer success to scope training engagements, support onboarding and enablement, and turn training into adoption and expansion.

  • Build relationships with law enforcement and industry partners across the region to grow the TRM Academy cadre and learner community.

  • Develop train-the-trainer materials and instructor guides so the Academy can scale in EMEA and coach other instructors as the team grows.

What We're Looking For

  • 3-5+ years of experience instructing courses, leading trainings, or delivering technical instruction.

  • Blockchain, cryptocurrency, or digital assets subject matter expertise (core requirement), ideally from hands-on on-chain investigations or crypto-enabled crime casework.

  • Law enforcement or government experience, or a proven track record training these audiences. Police and financial crime investigators are especially welcome.

  • Eligibility to obtain a government security clearance in the UK or another EMEA country.

  • Fluent English, written and spoken.

  • Experience building coursework, curriculum, labs, and appropriate testing.

  • Comfortable training private-sector audiences, such as crypto businesses/VASPs, exchanges, and financial institutions.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills and the ability to command the room.

  • Willingness and ability to travel 50-75% across EMEA.

  • AI fluency (part of our performance review process and of the interview process).

Nice to Have

  • Professional fluency in German (strongly preferred, given the size of our DACH opportunity).

  • Fluency in French, or in a Nordic, Baltic, or Eastern European language.

  • An existing national security clearance.

  • Experience in or alongside a national security, intelligence, or financial intelligence unit.

  • Working knowledge of cyber investigations, OSINT, and/or cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tradecraft.

  • Relevant certifications (for example GIAC credentials such as GCTI or GOSI, or similar cyber and OSINT credentials).

  • A Nordic, Baltic, or Eastern European background in crypto, particularly with national security experience.

A Note on AI Fluency

TRM is an AI-native company. We expect our instructors to already be using AI tools in their day-to-day work to accelerate research, author and refine training content, and speed up investigative and analytical workflows. AI fluency is not awareness or interest; it is production usage. It is evaluated in our interview process and is part of our performance review process.

Why This Role Matters

Investigators and analysts across Europe are facing crypto-enabled crime at growing scale, from fraud and ransomware to sanctions evasion and terrorism finance. By teaching them to trace funds on TRM's platforms and combine that with cyber and OSINT tradecraft, you directly increase how quickly and confidently they can detect, investigate, and disrupt the threats that put people at risk. Every cohort you train turns abstract concepts into concrete skills they can apply to active cases that week, and you will help define how TRM Academy shows up across EMEA.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

data.description:
Location: Any MSF office*

Contract: 100%

Duration: 12 months

Starting date: 04th of January 2027

Deadline to apply: 01st of December 2026

Compensation and Benefits: MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

MSF International

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

I. CONTEXT

MSF consists of 6 Operational Centres (OCs) and 3 European Supply Centres (ESCs). In the supply domain there is a joint Supply Tansformational Topics Roadmap composed by several inter-OC and inter-ESC projects, and their number is growing due to the need to increase cooperation between MSF entities while improving the quality of MSF's supply chain. The capacity to measure performance and analyse data across different entities is therefore essential and is contributing to MSF ambitions on interoperability and climate.

The role of the International Office is to foster cooperation and coordination between MSF entities. The Supply Data Analyst will therefore act as a facilitator between the OCs and ESCs: bringing their representatives together, helping them build shared approaches on supply data and performance, and turning these agreements into concrete deliverables.

The Global Supply Data & Analytics (GSDA) team (previously SCPM) has been actively working to build the analytical and data foundations needed to support a global approach to supply chain performance management, and to contribute to the governance of supply data across entities. The team is led by the Supply Chain Analytics Manager and includes one Data Analysts and one data governance specialist; the Supply Data Analyst will join it as an additional analyst.

Reporting hierarchically and functionally to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager, the Supply Data Analyst will: collaborate closely with the supply chain professionals responsible for BI and performance management within the 6 OCs and 3 ESCs; work in close link with the ShARP (Shared Analytics and Reporting Project) team in SITS (Shared IT Services); on the existing UniField intersection reports; work alongside the GSDA team and the IO Supply team on projects related to supply chain data analytics; and interact with stakeholders across MSF, including finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics and operations teams.

II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Supply Data Analyst supports supply chain performance analysis and decision making across MSF by delivering reliable data, KPIs, reports and actionable recommendations. The position also fosters cooperation between the OCs and ESCs around shared supply data, turning agreements into concrete deliverables.

Within GSDA, the Supply Data Analyst will support the growing need for data management, reporting and analytics from the supply chain teams, including the monitoring of KPIs and the analysis of data coming from MSF information systems (such as UniField, Isystock or Akiba).

III. ACCOUNTABILITIES

The Supply Data Analyst is accountable for the following expected results and the activities deployed to achieve them.

1. UniField intersection reports are reliable, relevant and meet the needs of the OCs

a. Take over the existing UniField intersection reports in close link with the ShARP team and improve them (reliability, relevance, usability) based on users' feedback and identified gaps

b. Collect the reporting needs of each OC and consolidate them into a clear, prioritised set of requirements

c. Design and deliver new intersection reports in coordination with the ShARP team, with validation from the OC representatives

2. Supply data is available and of reliable quality for analysis

a. Extract, clean and consolidate supply data from UniField and other information systems

b. Check data consistency and quality, and report anomalies to the relevant teams

c. Document data sources, definitions and calculation methods

3. KPIs and reporting solutions support decision making

a. Calculate and update a set of KPIs on a regular basis, in coordination with the teams concerned

b. Build and maintain ad hoc data reporting solutions (Power BI) providing visuals that accurately summarise supply chain activities while providing actionable insights

c. Support the teams in the definition of additional KPIs as needs arise

4. Stakeholders receive relevant data analysis and actionable recommendations

a. Support stakeholders on supply data analysis

b. Respond to ad hoc data and analysis requests using supply data from different stakeholders (supply, finance, medical…)

c. Present analysis results and recommendations in a clear way to non-technical audiences

5. Cooperation between the OCs and ESCs on supply data produces concrete deliverables

a. Convene and facilitate working groups and meetings with representatives of each OC and ESC, from preparation (agenda, pre-alignment of positions) to follow-up (minutes, actions, deadlines)

b. Lead discussions between entities with different needs and practices, and build compromises and consensus on shared definitions, KPIs and ways of working

c. Turn agreements into concrete deliverables (e.g., shared KPI definitions, dashboards, documentation) and follow their delivery

6. Data-related tools and processes improve continuously and stakeholders are kept informed

a. Contribute to the improvement of data-related tools and processes within the team

b. Proactively identify data needs, risks and improvement opportunities, and propose solutions autonomously

c. Manage stakeholders and expectations: identify their needs, keep them informed, and escalate blockers to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager when needed

IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY

Challenges and decisions that the job faces to achieve the accountabilities:

  • Autonomy to think and act: works with limited supervision; takes initiative, prioritises and drives work to completion, proactively identifies data needs, risks and improvement opportunities, and escalates blockers to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager when needed.

  • Complexity of the environment: works across 6 OCs and 3 ESCs with different needs, practices and information systems (UniField, Isystock, Akiba); builds compromises on shared definitions and KPIs, handles multiple priorities at once, and interacts with technical and non-technical stakeholders (finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics, operations) in a cross-cultural and cross-functional environment.

SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.


Education

  • Bachelor's level or above in data analytics, statistics, business management, supply chain or a related field, or a combination of relevant education and professional experience (essential)

Experience

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience as Data Analyst (essential)

  • Direct work experience involving significant data management (essential)

  • Experience in facilitating meetings or working groups involving multiple stakeholders and in delivering concrete outputs from them (essential)

  • Supply chain, logistics and Finance experience in NGO's operational settings (desirable)

  • Previous work experience with UniField, MSF's main ERP software (desirable)

Skills

  • Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills: ability to bring together representatives of different entities, lead effective meetings, negotiate compromises and deliver concrete outcomes

  • Strong analytical skills

  • Good organisational skills, ability to handle multiple priorities at one time

  • Autonomous and proactive: ability to take initiative, prioritise and drive work to completion with limited supervision

  • Good level skills in Excel, Power BI and database management

  • Ability to work in a cross-cultural and cross-functional environment

  • Drive for change, improvement and innovation

Languages

  • Fluent spoken and written English (essential)

  • Good command of French (strongly desirable)

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.

This is an Atlantic porfolio company.

The opportunity

Demand for AI compute is outrunning the infrastructure to deliver it, and the environmental bill is growing with it: more fossil power, more freshwater, more land. New capacity on land also means waiting years for power, sites and permits.

We take a different route: we bring compute to the power. Far offshore, the wind blows stronger and steadier than anywhere on land, and no grid will ever reach it. Using it lets AI scale without adding carbon or competing with communities and nature for water and land.

We're building fleets of autonomous ships that turn that wind into AI compute at sea. Each ship carries its own wind turbines and computing on board, and navigates on its own across the open ocean, following the strongest and steadiest winds. No mooring, no cables to shore: the fleet goes where the energy is. It's AI infrastructure built from the ground up for the open ocean, from power systems and autonomy to high-density computing, engineered to run in one of the harshest environments on Earth. No grid queue. No freshwater. No land. Zero-carbon compute that scales with the fleet.

  • Firm, low-carbon power at a target cost of ~€50/MWh, one of the biggest costs in running AI compute

  • 70%+ capacity factor: offshore wind that behaves like baseload

  • First demonstrator at sea in late 2027

Founded in 2025 by repeat entrepreneurs and industrial leaders. Backed by major international investors.

The mandate

You'll work directly with the CEO and the board and own the company's business strategy as we go from first demonstrator to fleet.

Our platform opens several paths to value across compute and infrastructure, from capacity to hardware to the services around them. You'll decide which to pursue first, build them into the core of the company, and open new ones as the fleet grows.

What you'll own

  • Business model & strategy. Shape the business model and evolve it as we scale: products, markets, pricing and unit economics. Turn a breakthrough technology into a bankable one.

  • Strategic partnerships. Decide which partners and customers we build the company with, from AI labs and cloud providers to chipmakers and sovereign compute programmes, and secure the relationships that shape our first fleet.

  • Capital strategy. Work with the CEO on how the business case underpins project finance and fundraising, and own that story with investors and the board.

  • Product direction. Make sure what we build at sea is shaped by where the market is going, working hand in hand with our marine, power and systems engineers.

  • Ecosystem & alliances. Build the partnerships a new infrastructure class needs: chip and systems vendors, cloud platforms, data center operators, ports and financiers.

  • Category leadership. Be our external voice on summit stages, with policymakers and in the press, and make us the reference for AI infrastructure at sea.

  • The business organisation. Build and lead the team across strategy, partnerships and commercial that takes us from demonstrator to fleet.

Who you are

  • You've built businesses in deep tech or infrastructure. You've led strategy, business development or a P&L in AI, cloud, data centers or semiconductors, and shaped large, multi-year partnerships.

  • You've taken frontier technology to market. You've brought new, capital-intensive technology to its first major customers and closed the off-take agreements, capacity reservations or long-term contracts that made it bankable.

  • You build, not just run. You've built something from zero, whether a company, a business line or a market, and you're at your best when the playbook doesn't exist yet.

  • You see the whole board. You move between unit economics, partnerships, financing and long-term strategy in the same afternoon.

  • You know AI infrastructure from the inside. Compute economics, workload constraints, and where the market is heading.

  • Compute and infrastructure are your world. GPUs, data centers, power and the economics that tie them together. You hold your own with engineers and turn technical depth into business strategy.

  • The mission matters to you. A business built on AI infrastructure at sea excites you, and you want your work to help AI grow without costing the planet.

  • You work in English. Fluent English is required; French is a plus.

How you operate

  • Ownership. You treat the company's outcomes as your own, well beyond your remit.

  • First principles. You reason from the economics and the physics, not from how the market has always worked.

  • Bold and rigorous. You make big bets and do the work to back them.

  • AI-native. You use modern tools to think, decide and move faster.

Why this role

  • A C-level mandate across strategy, product and capital, working directly with the CEO and the board

  • The chance to define how compute infrastructure at sea becomes a business, and to keep redefining it as it scales

  • An uncompromising team of repeat entrepreneurs and industrial leaders, backed by top-tier international capital

  • Based wherever you do your best work, with a global mandate and flexible hours. Our home port is Nantes.

Dates : 6 mois à partir de février ou mars 2027

Contexte du projet :

L’allègement des structures automobiles reste un levier majeur pour réduire la consommation et les émissions des véhicules, tout en répondant à des exigences croissantes de rigidité et de tenue au crash. Les pièces de caisse en blanc sont en grande majorité réalisées à partir de tôles d’acier mises en forme, dont la conception repose encore largement sur l’expertise et sur des itérations successives entre calcul et dessin.

L’optimisation topologique permet de déterminer la meilleure répartition de matière dans un domaine de conception donné. Appliquée à un domaine volumique 3D, elle conduit cependant à des structures massives ou de type treillis, difficilement transposables en pièces embouties d’épaisseur quasi constante. Le défi scientifique consiste à formuler une méthode capable de faire émerger, à partir d’un domaine volumique, des géométries représentatives de tôles (structures à parois minces), en maîtrisant l’épaisseur et la fabricabilité, sous chargements statiques puis dynamiques.

Ce stage s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une collaboration de recherche entre le LTDS et ArcelorMittal Global R&D. Il a vocation à se poursuivre par une thèse CIFRE en cas de résultats concluants.

L’objectif du stage sera de développer et d’évaluer une première méthodologie d’optimisation topologique 3D aboutissant à une solution en tôle d’acier, en s’appuyant sur une structure automobile.

Les missions pourront comprendre :

•Un état de l’art des méthodes d’optimisation topologique conduisant à des structures minces de type coque (contrôle d’épaisseur par filtrage et projection, contraintes de longueur caractéristique, approches par composants explicites ou level-set).

•Le développement d’un algorithme d’optimisation 3D appliqué à une pièce automobile soumise à des chargements statiques.

•L’extension de la méthode à des solutions plus avancées proposées par ArcelorMittal.

Les missions pourront être adaptées en fonction du profil du candidat et de l’avancement du projet.


Profil recherché : étudiant(e) en Master 2 ou équivalent (stage ingénieur) dans le domaine de la mécanique numérique, du calcul des structures ou des mathématiques appliquées.

Compétences souhaitées : méthode des éléments finis, optimisation numérique, programmation scientifique (Python, MATLAB ou C++). Des connaissances en optimisation topologique ou en dynamique rapide (LS-DYNA, Radioss) seront appréciées.

Encadrement : Frédéric Gillot (LTDS, École Centrale de Lyon) ; Daoming Yu, Alexandre Blaise et Cristian Alvarez (ArcelorMittal Global R&D).

L’accueil au laboratoire est soumis à une autorisation préalable (procédure FSD, 2 à 3 mois de délai) : les candidatures (CV, lettre de motivation, relevés de notes) sont à adresser dès que possible.

Contexte du rôle

Le ou la Team Lead Solution Consulting est responsable de l’organisation, de la performance et du développement de l’équipe de Solution Consultants.

L’équipe intervient auprès des clients Pennylane sur la dimension fonctionnelle de projets en cours : analyse des besoins, cadrage, mise en œuvre, formation et adoption du produit.

Par son management, sa coordination et son pilotage de la capacité, le ou la Team Lead veille à ce que les clients bénéficient d’un accompagnement de qualité, au bon moment et avec le niveau d’expertise attendu.

Missions principales

  • Manager et développer l’équipe Solution Consulting : définir les objectifs individuels et collectifs, organiser les rituels de management, accompagner la montée en compétences, donner du feedback et suivre la performance. Veiller à l’engagement, à la motivation et à la dynamique collective.

  • Organiser et optimiser le staffing de l’équipe : consolider les besoins liés aux projets en cours, anticiper la charge, répartir les missions en fonction des compétences et des disponibilités, et s’assurer que les ressources sont mobilisées au bon moment et sur les bons sujets.

  • Définir les règles de priorisation et anticiper les tensions de capacité : construire des principes de priorisation et de staffing partagés avec les équipes Sales et les autres parties prenantes, arbitrer les demandes concurrentes, identifier les risques de surcharge ou de sous-capacité et alerter en cas de risque sur les délais ou la qualité.

  • Superviser l’efficacité opérationnelle et la performance de l’équipe : définir et suivre les indicateurs clés de l’activité, notamment la couverture des besoins, les délais de staffing, la charge de l’équipe, le respect des engagements, la qualité des accompagnements et les difficultés liées à la coordination ou à la capacité.

  • Garantir les standards de qualité et les méthodes de travail : définir et faire évoluer les bonnes pratiques applicables à l’analyse fonctionnelle, au cadrage, aux ateliers, aux formations, à la documentation et aux livrables produits par l’équipe.

  • Coordonner les parties prenantes internes : faciliter la collaboration entre les Solution Consultants, les équipes Sales et Account Management, les PrM ou équipes Delivery, les CSM, Solution Engineering, Produit, Support, Operations et People.

  • Développer l’amélioration continue de la fonction : analyser les retours terrain, identifier les irritants, faire évoluer les outils, les processus et les modes de fonctionnement, et faciliter la contribution de l’équipe aux demandes prioritaires, notamment aux réponses à des appels d’offres lorsque l’expertise fonctionnelle est requise et que la demande est priorisée selon les enjeux business.

Profil recherché

  • Vous justifiez d’au moins 2 ans d’expérience en management de proximité et dans l’accompagnement d’une équipe.

  • Vous avez une expérience dans le pilotage d’une activité impliquant plusieurs projets, ressources, niveaux d’expertise et parties prenantes.

  • Vous disposez d’une bonne compréhension des environnements de conseil fonctionnel, de déploiement logiciel, de formation, de Customer Success ou de Professional Services.

  • Vous maîtrisez les enjeux de capacity planning, de staffing, d’allocation des ressources et de gestion de la charge.

  • Vous savez définir des objectifs, suivre la performance, donner du feedback et accompagner les évolutions professionnelles.

  • Vous êtes capable de structurer des processus, des standards et des méthodes de travail dans un environnement en évolution.

  • Vous êtes à l’aise avec le pilotage par les données et la construction d’indicateurs opérationnels pertinents.

  • Vous savez prioriser, arbitrer et prendre des décisions dans un contexte de demandes concurrentes.

  • Vous disposez d’excellentes capacités de communication, de coordination et d’influence auprès d’équipes aux responsabilités différentes.

  • Vous êtes orienté vers la qualité de l’expérience client, pragmatique, attentif au collectif et engagé dans l’amélioration continue.

🇫🇷 Données personnelles

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer & gérer un vivier de candidats. Vous pouvez vous opposer à tout moment et demander la suppression de vos données en écrivant à :
Notre data policy
